data.narrative:
Lila Sciences is a Series A biotech company founded by Geoffrey von Maltzahn and Molly Gibson, having raised $200M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 3 public peers in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private-stage companies, though direct peer multiples are constrained by data availability.

Of three valuation methods assessed, only stage-progression analysis proved applicable. This method uses the $200M total raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression, yielding an implied valuation of $400M. Peer-median triangulation was not executable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum thresholds (fewer than 3 datapoints after filtering). Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples could not be applied because target revenue is not disclosed, a constraint common to private biotech companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $340M to $460M, with a median of $400M. This range reflects a single methodology and carries meaningful uncertainty. Key risks include the reliance on stage-progression as the sole quantitative input, absence of revenue data for public multiple validation, and limited comparable trading data for Series A biotech. Additional disclosure of financial metrics or identification of tighter peer cohorts would improve precision.
